source_refs.note: Limitations: a main subheading of 28.3 Thin-Layer Chromatography, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 179-181.

items: TLC is mainly a qualitative technique and can only give an idea about the amount of a substance. So, TLC is not accurate and precise quantitative technique.
TLC cannot clearly separate compounds having close Rf values. Hence resolution of spots is not always high and sharp.
In TLC, only small amounts of sample can be applied and analysed. It is not suitable for large-scale separation.
This technique is sensitive to humidity, temperature and cleanliness of working environment which reduces reproducibility.

blocks.title: Quick Check 28.1
blocks.text:
a) A mixture contains butanone and pentane. How can they be separated by using thin layer chromatography using aluminium oxide as stationary phase and benzene as solvent?
b) A mixture of two substances X and Y is analysed by thin-layer chromatography. The Rf value of substance X is larger than that of substance Y. Suggest why substance X has a larger Rf value.
c) A separate thin layer chromatography experiment was done using the hair dyes A, B and C. The chromatogram obtained is shown. State three conclusions about the hair dyes A, B and C which vcan be deduced from the chromatogram.

blocks.alt: A chromatogram of three hair dyes. Dye A gives one spot low on the plate, dye B one spot high on the plate, and dye C two spots, one at the height of A's spot and one at the height of B's.
blocks.caption: Quick Check 28.1(c): Chromatogram of the hair dyes A, B and C (original drawing after the chromatogram printed in Quick Check 28.1).
